# Shading and Lighting Models

Also called: 3D Gaussian Splatting Shading, Gaussian Splatting Lighting, Gaussian Splatting Relighting

## Overview
Shading and Lighting Models define how 3D Gaussian primitives are composited into a 2D image, addressing the limitations of standard front-to-back [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) which requires strict depth sorting and assumes non-overlapping primitives. These models range from hybrid approaches that balance performance and accuracy to analytic volumetric integration that eliminates projection artifacts, and order-independent methods that bypass sorting entirely. They extend standard [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) rendering](#2063-gaussian-splatting-volume-rendering.md) to support dynamic, physically-based lighting and self-occlusion, solving the inability of standard 3DGS to support real-time environment changes or accurate shadows due to baked lighting in [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) or fixed forward shading.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on 3D Gaussian primitives defined by mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$ (or scales and orientation), opacity $o$, and color $\mathbf{c}$ (or spherical harmonic coefficients). The core challenge is computing the pixel color $C$ and accumulated alpha $\alpha$ given a camera ray. Standard [splatting](#23-splatting.md) projects 3D Gaussians to 2D ellipses, computes a 2D alpha mask, and blends them in screen space. These models modify the blending or shading stage: some refine the depth metric used for sorting, others integrate the 3D density function directly along the ray, and others use weighted averages to bypass sorting. All assume the Gaussians are sorted or processed in a manner that approximates front-to-back accumulation to ensure correct occlusion.

For relighting, splats must carry physical material attributes: normal, roughness, reflectance (specular strength), and albedo (diffuse color) [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md]. These are stored in a parallel Material Buffer aligned with the Splat Buffer [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].

For self-shadowing, a virtual "sun camera" is constructed to simulate a directional light source [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md]. This camera is placed at a large distance with a narrow field of view (FOV) to minimize parallax error to below 2% [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

Both relighting (for cache locality) and shadowing (for correct front-to-back accumulation) require sorting. Relighting uses spatial locality algorithms like Morton codes [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md]. Shadowing sorts Gaussians by depth relative to the sun camera [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

During the light pass for shadowing, the projection covariance is not expanded by $0.3I$ and no amplitude compensation is applied, preserving the main camera pass's sampling expansion [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md]. In shadowing calculations, sun camera framing, sorting, coverage, and threshold branches are treated as constants to prevent incorrect gradient propagation [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

## Subtopics

### [Analytic-Splatting Forward Shading](3459-analytic-splatting-forward-shading.md)
Computes the 2D Gaussian signal response for a pixel by performing eigendecomposition on the projected covariance matrix, rotating the coordinate system to decouple axes, and applying a conditioned logistic function to approximate the pixel area integral of the Gaussian CDF. It differs from standard 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) by replacing the simple Gaussian evaluation at the pixel center with an [analytic integration](#9001-trapezoid-based-radiance-integration-in-box-coordinates.md) approximation, and from Mip-Splatting by using a logistic function approximation rather than a Mip-NeRF-inspired cone integral, thereby achieving state-of-the-art detail fidelity under multiscale and super-resolution settings at the cost of increased computational operations.

### [Transparency and Blending Models](9274-transparency-and-blending-models.md)
Define how 3D Gaussian primitives are composited into a 2D image, addressing the limitations of standard [front-to-back alpha blending](#1141-front-to-back-compositing-unpremultiplied.md) which requires strict depth sorting and assumes non-overlapping primitives. These models range from hybrid approaches that balance performance and accuracy to analytic volumetric integration that eliminates projection artifacts, and order-independent methods that bypass sorting entirely.

### [Lighting, Shadowing & Relighting](11894-lighting-shadowing-relighting.md)
Extends 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) rendering to support dynamic, physically-based lighting and self-occlusion. Standard 3DGS bakes lighting into spherical harmonics (SH) or uses fixed forward shading, preventing real-time environment changes or accurate shadows. These methods solve that by either deferring material attributes to a G-buffer for split-sum environment map integration or by performing a dedicated light-space rasterization pass to compute front-facing [transmittance for self-shadowing](#2441-volume-cloud-self-shadowing-via-ray-marching.md).
